notes: Use Tailwind CSS utility classes exclusively over hand-written CSS files; co-locate design tokens as Tailwind theme extensions (colors, fontFamily, borderRadius) rather than scattering hex values through components. lucide-react for icons, motion (Framer Motion) for animation.

Keep the design system reference short enough to fit in a single prompt phase (under ~1000 words) — express it as named tokens/utility classes Cursor can apply consistently across files rather than a long prose description it has to re-derive each time.

Front-load the full design token set and component conventions in the initial context; Claude Code can carry and apply a large system consistently across many files in one session, so it's worth being exhaustive rather than terse.

Both tools generate from component-level prompts — describe visual states (empty/loading/error/success) and exact Tailwind classes per component rather than describing the system abstractly; these tools respond best to concrete, copyable examples.

Express design rules as hard directives/invariants (Cascade memories) rather than suggestions — e.g. 'All buttons use rounded-lg, all cards use border-slate-200' as fixed rules Cascade should check itself against.

Keep the design system's dependency footprint minimal (avoid heavyweight animation/chart libraries) since Bolt's WebContainer sandbox is sensitive to install size and time; prefer CSS transitions over a JS animation library where the motion tier is 'subtle'.

Write the design system as a fully self-contained, tool-agnostic reference document (tokens, rationale, states) since the target implementation tool and its conventions are unknown — avoid tool-specific syntax.

Prefer CSS variables for design tokens defined in globals.css and consumed via Tailwind's theme() where possible, so tokens work identically in Server and Client Components; keep motion/animation strictly in Client Components.

Express the palette as a Color asset catalog (supporting light/dark variants natively) and typography via the Dynamic Type text style system rather than fixed point sizes; prefer SF Symbols over any custom icon set for platform-native feel.

Encode the design system as a ThemeData/ColorScheme object so Material and Cupertino widgets both inherit it consistently; define TextTheme entries for the full type scale rather than styling text ad hoc per widget.

Same conventions as Vite + React (this target compiles to that stack) — additionally keep all Gemini API calls server-side per the platform's port-3000/server.ts convention, never referencing API keys from styled client components.

Design tokens should avoid any CSS-only concept (no box-shadow, no CSS gradients as strings) — express elevation via platform-appropriate shadow/elevation props and gradients via a library (expo-linear-gradient) from the start.
